title: Beyond Coverage and Mutation: A Blind-Spot Analysis of LLM-Generated Unit Tests
abstract: arXiv:2610.32548v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing evaluation protocols for unit tests rely on aggregate metrics such as branch coverage and mutation score. These metrics quantify the extent to which a test suite exercises program behavior, but do not identify the behavioral obligations it systematically leaves unchecked. We propose BlindSpotEval, an obligation-based evaluation framework aligned with the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern. The framework comprises three metrics, Boundary-Value Adequacy, Control-Flow Adequacy, and Oracle Strength, complemented by an assessment of execution reliability. We also introduce ObligBench, a complexity-stratified Java benchmark comprising 895 complex and 700 low-complexity functions with source-side obligation annotations. Evaluating 14,320 tests from four LLMs under four prompting strategies reveals systematic blind spots. Incorrect assertions account for 15.6% of test failures, illustrating that coverage alone does not establish oracle correctn

translated_title: 超越覆盖率与变异得分：LLM生成单元测试的盲点分析
translated_abstract: 现有的单元测试评估协议依赖于分支覆盖率和变异得分等聚合指标。这些指标衡量的是测试套件对程序行为的覆盖程度，但无法识别测试套件系统性地遗漏检查的行为义务。我们提出了BlindSpotEval，一个与Arrange-Act-Assert（准备-执行-断言）模式对齐的基于义务的评估框架。该框架包含三个指标：边界值充分性、控制流充分性和断言强度，并辅以对执行可靠性的评估。我们还引入了ObligBench，这是一个按复杂度分层的Java基准，包含895个复杂函数和700个低复杂度函数，并带有源代码侧的义务标注。对来自四个大语言模型在四种提示策略下生成的14,320个测试用例的评估揭示了系统性的盲点：错误断言占测试失败总数的15.6%，这表明仅凭覆盖率并不能保证断言（预言）的正确性。
tldr: 该论文提出了基于行为义务的单元测试评估框架BlindSpotEval和配套Java基准ObligBench，通过边界值充分性、控制流充分性和断言强度三个指标揭示了大语言模型生成单元测试的系统性盲点，发现错误断言占测试失败的15.6%，证明覆盖率无法保证断言正确性。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes BlindSpotEval, an obligation-based evaluation framework with three metrics (Boundary-Value Adequacy, Control-Flow Adequacy, and Oracle Strength) and ObligBench, a complexity-stratified Java benchmark, revealing systematic blind spots in LLM-generated unit tests where incorrect assertions account for 15.6% of test failures, demonstrating that coverage alone does not establish oracle correctness.
